name: Tacony–Palmyra Bridge
facts: The Tacony–Palmyra Bridge, designed by Polish-born Ralph Modjeski, opened on August 14, 1929, replacing a ferry that had operated since 1922 and spanning 3,659 feet across the Delaware River.
In 2013, a maintenance roller seized, jamming the bascule span in the open position and shutting the bridge for eleven hours, a rare but dramatic event in its history.
Rebuilt in 1997, the bridge now carries three wide lanes—two northbound toward Philadelphia and one southbound—while a pedestrian walkway invites cyclists and walkers.
